# phasetwo_cluster_domain (Resource)

A custom hostname on a dedicated cluster.

Creating this registers the hostname and starts DNS validation. It does **not** create DNS records for you — read `domain_records` and create them at your DNS provider, after which Phase Two validates the domain and issues a certificate.

Adding a domain does not start serving traffic on it. Once its certificate is issued, point `phasetwo_cluster_primary_host` at it.

~> Part of domain provisioning can involve a manual step on the Phase Two side, so `wait_for_certificate` is off by default. Turning it on can block an apply for a long time.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "phasetwo_cluster_domain" "auth" {
  cluster_id = phasetwo_cluster.main.id
  host       = "auth.example.com"
}

# Phase Two validates the domain by DNS. Create the records it asks for — here with the AWS
# provider, but any DNS provider works.
resource "aws_route53_record" "validation" {
  for_each = {
    for record in phasetwo_cluster_domain.auth.domain_records : record.name => record
  }

  zone_id = var.zone_id
  name    = each.value.name
  type    = each.value.type
  records = [each.value.value]
  ttl     = 60
}

# Waiting for the certificate is off by default, because issuance depends on the DNS records
# above. Do it in a separate resource that depends on them, or simply apply twice.
output "certificate_status" {
  value = phasetwo_cluster_domain.auth.certificate_status
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) ID of the cluster. The cluster must be `ACTIVE`.
- `host` (String) The custom hostname, e.g. `auth.example.com`.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `wait_for_certificate` (Boolean) Block until the TLS certificate is issued. Off by default, because issuance waits on DNS records that Terraform has not created yet — turning it on in the same apply that creates those records will deadlock. Use it in a later apply, or with a `depends_on` covering your DNS resources.

### Read-Only

- `certificate_status` (String) TLS certificate status. The domain can serve traffic once this is `ISSUED`.
- `created_at` (String) When the domain was added, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.
- `domain_records` (Attributes List) DNS records to create in order to validate the domain. Empty once validation has completed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--domain_records))
- `id` (String) Unique identifier of the custom domain.
- `organization_id` (String) ID of the organization that owns the cluster.
- `status` (String) DNS validation status: `PENDING_VALIDATION`, `SUCCESS`, `FAILED` or `NOT_FOUND`.
- `type` (String) What the hostname is used for: `WEB` or `MAIL`.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).


<a id="nestedatt--domain_records"></a>
### Nested Schema for `domain_records`

Read-Only:

- `name` (String) Record name.
- `type` (String) Record type, e.g. `CNAME`.
- `value` (String) Record value.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import phasetwo_cluster_domain.auth 4f8c1e2a-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/7d2e9f10-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
```
